parts:
[moved to stan-dev; removed issue comment on GitHub]

Everyone: please keep the issue tracker comments relevant
to the issue where you're commenting. In particular, please
don't hijack them with new issues, even if you think they're
related. Instead, please either (a) start a discussion on the
stan-dev group, or (b) create a new issue.

If you create a new issue, it should be concrete in terms of
what the intended *behavior* is. That is, the issue body should
be a functional spec. You don't need to go into how to implement
it, but it's OK if you do.

Thanks,

- Bob

> On Mar 24, 2016, at 4:48 PM, Andrew Gelman <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
>
> Hi, let me take this as a reminder that we should be cleaning up the Stan output. When I run Stan from R it fills up the console with these messages, it’s quite annoying and also who needs to see every tenth, anyway. We can discuss sometime at Stan meeting. My suggestion from before, which I still like, is to just spit out one message after 10% of warmup iterations giving estimated total time, maybe another after 10% of the sampling iterations with an updated estimated time, since they can be faster than warmup. Also we should have a no-print option, I think.
> A
